QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_8

question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III) has AUM of INR 500 cr and a daily volatility of 1.2%. Using parametric VaR with the standard 1.645 z-score, what is the 95% 1-day VaR?

explanation.text: The Logic: Parametric VaR(95%, 1-day) = z × σ × AUM = 1.645 × 1.2% × 500 cr = INR 9.87 crore. i.e., there is a 95% probability the fund will NOT lose more than ~INR 9.87 cr in one day. The Trap: INR 13.96 cr uses 2.33 z-score (that's 99%). INR 6 cr uses 1σ (≈84% conf). INR 60 cr uses a 10σ assumption. Using the wrong confidence-level z is the #1 VaR exam trap. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) tests portfolio VaR too. XIX-E frames VaR in Cat III fund-risk policy with 99% regulatory reporting. Manager's Pro-Tip: Parametric VaR assumes normality and underestimates fat tails. Augment with historical VaR and Expected Shortfall (CVaR) — regulators increasingly want CVaR on Cat III quarterly risk reports.
